title: Community supervision remains a large state-contact system even as its population declines
source_unit: Bureau of Justice Statistics Annual Probation Survey and Annual Parole Survey, Probation and Parole in the United States, 2024
geography: United States probation and parole agencies

observations.period: January 1 through December 31, 2024; yearend 2014 to yearend 2024

denominator.unit: BJS community-supervision population estimates and comparable-agency comparison

comparable_agency_2024_change.unit: percent change from January 1 to December 31, 2024

comparable_agency_decade_change.unit: percent change from yearend 2014 to yearend 2024

exit_categories.value: completion, incarceration, absconding, and other unsatisfactory outcomes
exit_categories.unit: reported types of movement off supervision

later_life_outcomes.unit: work, housing, family, health, trust, safety, and political participation after supervision

observations.method: BJS Annual Probation Survey and Annual Parole Survey estimates, with comparable-agency population changes and administrative movement categories kept separate from person-level wellbeing or causal outcomes.
observations.uncertainty: The national estimate and the comparable-agency decade comparison have different coverage and comparison frames. Aggregate supervision counts do not identify supervision intensity, condition burden, service receipt, or unique-person trajectories.
observations.subgroup: Adults under probation or parole; the report provides characteristics such as sex, race or ethnicity, and most serious offense, but this record does not infer subgroup mechanisms or later outcomes.
observations.counterinterpretation: A declining supervision population may reflect changes in sentencing, admissions, releases, policy, reporting, or other factors; a smaller population does not establish lighter supervision, lower burden, or better reintegration.

boundary: This record adds the scale, decline, movement categories, and continuing state-contact surface of community supervision. It does not follow the same person through conditions, services, violation or completion, housing, work, family life, safety, trust, political action, or durable inclusion.
